explain.say: A bicycle standing still falls over, yet when it is moving it seems to balance itself. The main secret is steering: a moving bike is constantly steered back under its own weight.

faq.q: How does steering keep a bike balanced?
faq.a: When the bike leans one way, steering the same way moves the wheels back under the centre of mass, stopping the fall. Riders make these small corrections all the time.
asks: How do you balance on a bike?

faq.q: Can a bicycle balance without a rider?
faq.a: Yes. A riderless bike pushed at the right speed can stay upright for a while, because its design makes the front wheel steer into any lean. It falls when it slows down.
asks: Why does a bike stay up by itself?

faq.q: What is trail on a bicycle?
faq.a: Trail is the distance on the ground between where the front tyre touches and where the steering axis would meet the ground. With the tyre behind that point, the front wheel tends to swing into a lean.
asks: Why is the front fork angled?

faq.q: Why is it easier to balance a bike when going faster?
faq.a: At speed, small steering movements quickly shift the wheels back under you, and the bike self-corrects more strongly. At very low speed there is little time and little self-steering.

faq.q: Is a bike kept up by its spinning wheels like a gyroscope?
faq.a: The spinning wheels help a little by nudging the front wheel to steer into a lean, but they are not the main reason. Experiments show bikes can still balance with the gyroscopic effect cancelled out.
asks: Do gyroscopic forces keep a bike up?

facts: A riderless bicycle rolling at the right speed can stay upright by itself for a while.
In 2011 researchers built an experimental bicycle that balanced itself without gyroscopic effects or trail.
Riders balance mainly by steering the wheels back under their centre of mass.
